## CI triage on patch set 1: two REAL failures, neither an infra flake

`Verified -1` on change 1617 PS1 was not the known shallow-clone flake — it was two genuine
failures, both caused by main moving during the 40h strand. Reproduced locally after installing
the `reviewbot` extra (my earlier local run lacked fastapi, so the whole lifespan tier SKIPPED —
that gap is why the first push looked green).

### A. A real defect in the adopted design: the stop flag outlived its shutdown

`test_accepted_rerun_survives_restart_via_gerrit_reconcile` failed DETERMINISTICALLY on all four
lanes with `{'scanned': 1, 'reviewed': 0}`. Root cause: `_stop_requested` is module state on
`reconcile`, not per-app, and was cleared only at lifespan STARTUP. That test exits the lifespan
and then re-drives the rerun the discarded in-memory queue lost — the replacement-process
recovery path — so it ran `reconcile_once` with the flag still SET and the pass declined
everything.

This is a production defect, not a test artifact: after any lifespan shutdown, every later
`reconcile_once` in that process silently reviews nothing while still reporting the candidates as
`scanned`, so it reads as "nothing was owed a vote" rather than as a fault. That is precisely the
silent-backfill-failure mode 9ec0 exists to prevent. The flag now clears at the END of shutdown,
after the bounded cancel, so it cannot outlive the shutdown that set it. Added a test pinning the
post-shutdown state directly rather than only via that oracle's side effects.

Worth recording: the original commit's rationale said CI's pytest lane installs only `[dev]` so
the fastapi tier skips there. That is FALSE for this lane — CI ran 11945 tests including the
lifespan tier. The default-tier duplication was still worth having, but the stated reason for it
was wrong.

### B. A new wall-clock-assert lint, right about 3 of its 4 findings

Main grew `scripts/check_wall_clock_asserts.py` while this branch sat (upper-bound wall-clock
asserts are a proven flake class). Rather than blanket-sanctioning:

- The AC2 test's `elapsed < 3.0` was REDUNDANT and is gone: a drain that re-extended would have
  to start a second review, which its `len(started) == 1` already catches structurally.
- The shared-deadline and in-flight-gate tests now read the timeout the drain was actually
  HANDED, via a spy on the lifespan's `asyncio.wait`, instead of timing it. Strictly stronger — a
  stopwatch also passes if the wait runs and happens to return fast — and it fails in the SAFE
  direction, since a loaded runner leaves LESS budget remaining, never more. Both were
  mutation-checked (removed gate; independent window) and both go red.
- Only the idle-stop test keeps a ceiling, sanctioned as a hang-guard: its failure mode is
  waiting out a 3600s interval, so a 5s ceiling dwarfs the ~0.25s actually needed.

Gates on the new base: lint 0, typecheck 0, wall-clock 0, `test_review_bot.py` 104 passed / 0
skipped. Patch set 2 pushed.
